verdict: incident.io: Choose incident.io when incident command is the job and you want a published $15 Team floor — not PagerDuty by default, and not Datadog/Sentry. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
bestFor: Teams that want incident command in Slack more than a paging-first ops cloud
Buyers who will add on-call only if needed
Product-led incident response versus PagerDuty Professional seats
notIdealFor: Orgs whose primary job is PagerDuty-style on-call paging at enterprise scale
ITSM ticket desks without incident command
tradeoffs: Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models
Module stacking and consumption overages vs single-SKU floors
Free tiers vs enterprise SSO/audit gates
Landscape-adjacent tools vs primary job-cluster peers on best pages
recommendation: Choose incident.io when incident command is the job and you want a published $15 Team floor — not PagerDuty by default, and not Datadog/Sentry. Compare PagerDuty for paging-first on-call; Jira Service Management if Atlassian ITSM alerting is enough.
editorialNotes: IT industry Tier-A batch. Approved on it-development-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=incident-oncall. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Slack-native incident UX is approachable for modern SRE teams. Not a lab test.
Incident-oncall cluster — ranked with PagerDuty, not as an observability peer of Datadog or Sentry.

Slack/Teams-native incident workflows are the integration story.
Team/Pro are product-led; Enterprise carries heavier governance.
Per-user ladder plus Enterprise quote; held below PagerDuty’s scale story.
Free Basic plus $15 Team floor is a clear published entry; on-call add-on is the TCO catch. Affiliate economics excluded.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
